## Materials for today

- Coll 2013, *Private Empire: ExxonMobil and American Power*, ch. 4 & 18

**Overview.** In 2001, eleven Indonesian villagers sued ExxonMobil in U.S. federal court, alleging the company was complicit in human-rights abuses (murder, torture, rape) committed by Indonesian security forces that ExxonMobil had hired to protect its natural-gas extraction facility and pipeline in Aceh. The suit, brought under the Alien Tort Statute, has wound through U.S. courts for two decades; Exxon has since sold the Aceh fields to Indonesia's state oil company, Pertamina.

## In class

Working in your team, you'll apply the course's **assess → diagnose → propose** framework to this case and produce one written response per team. The specific discussion questions are distributed at the start of class.
